title: 4-day coke user was delirious: Coroner's report. Toronto man dies en route to hospital
article: A man on a four-day cocaine binge who died en route to a hospital after he was pepper-sprayed by Toronto police was probably suffering excited delirium, says Ontario's deputy chief coroner.

Jim Cairns said eyewitness accounts of a confrontation between police officers and Robert Walker early yesterday indicate the 41- year-old man had all the symptoms of excited delirium. "(People with excited delirium) have lost that control and are firing on all cylinders," Cairns said.

The rare medical condition may have been triggered by cocaine use that left Walker impervious to pain and close to death. The condition, which can also affect those with severe psychiatric illness or alcohol withdrawal, is characterized by bizarre behaviour, hallucinations, an incredible burst of strength and an elevated body temperature.
Toronto police are now being investigated by Ontario's Special Investigations Unit to determine if they played a role in Walker's death.

Neighbours said police were called to Walker's east-end home after the man reportedly went berserk on the fourth day of a cocaine spree. He was punching walls until his hands were left bloody. The confrontation quickly moved to a cordoned-off street, where Walker - naked in sub-zero temperatures - was surrounded by police who tried to subdue him with pepper spray, said witness Priya Glassey.
